isv-success-program.title: ISV Success – Microsoft Partner Center
isv-success-program.notes: ISV Success is a twelve-month program inside the Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program for software development companies. It is meant for firms that build business-to-business applications on or integrated with the Microsoft cloud and want to publish them in Microsoft Marketplace. To join, the company must not be headquartered in an embargoed country and needs an application project that is externally available, intended for recurring sales and has at least one assigned developer. Participants commit to start development within a few months, finish within the year and publish to the marketplace. The core package bundles Azure sponsorship credit, an Azure support plan, a Microsoft 365 developer subscription, Dynamics 365 sandboxes, Visual Studio Enterprise, GitHub Enterprise Cloud for new customers and one-to-one guidance on design, go-to-market and listing optimization. Benefits are activated in Partner Center under Benefits. Larger packages exist for existing participants and for companies with a certified software designation, but they depend on Microsoft's discretion. The program can be renewed for a further year once an offer has been published or made transactable and a renewal fee is paid. Sales and marketing benefits require a marketplace listing.

mail-flow-rule.title: Manage mail flow rules in Exchange Online – Microsoft Learn
mail-flow-rule.notes: Mail flow rules, also called transport rules, let an Exchange Online organization inspect messages passing through it and act on them when certain conditions match. A rule consists of conditions, actions and optional exceptions. Typical actions include prepending text to the subject, forwarding a message for approval, sending a policy tip to the sender or generating an incident report. Further settings cover the rule mode (enforce, or test with or without policy tips), a severity value that only filters reports, a time window for activation, a setting to stop processing further rules and a choice of whether to match the sender address in the header, the envelope or both. Rules are processed in priority order, with the top rule evaluated first. Admins can manage them in the Exchange admin center or with Exchange Online PowerShell, and rules created in the admin center start out disabled. The page shows an example that tags external mail sent to a distribution group. Changes can take a while to apply, report data can lag, and the page advises testing each rule and the combination of rules thoroughly.

microsoft-365-message-center.title: Manage Message center – Microsoft 365 admin
microsoft-365-message-center.notes: The Message center is a view in the Microsoft 365 admin center, found under Health, that informs IT admins about upcoming changes, feature updates and required actions across services. It is also reachable through the Microsoft 365 Admin mobile app with push notifications. Posts fall into three categories: prevent or fix issues, plan for change and stay informed. A relevance recommendation of high, medium or low is based on service usage and expected impact, and major updates are announced well ahead when action is required. For some features an organization-specific rollout status such as scheduled, rolling out or launched is shown. Admins can filter by service, tag, category and timing, pick which services appear, configure a weekly digest email and share posts or copy links. Archiving applies only to the individual admin account. Posts can be synced to Planner or read through the Microsoft Graph service communications API. Most admin roles can see the Message center, and a dedicated Message center reader role grants read and share access without other admin rights. Release status and usage figures are only available for part of the content.

microsoft-pluton.title: Microsoft Pluton security processor – Microsoft Learn
microsoft-pluton.notes: Microsoft Pluton is a cryptographic security processor integrated into the CPU or system-on-chip, made up of a secure hardware subsystem and Microsoft-owned software running on it. Microsoft designed it and silicon partners build it. Its purpose is to provide a hardware root of trust, secure identity, secure attestation and cryptographic services, protecting credentials, identities, personal data and encryption keys. It is meant to cover the functions of a Trusted Platform Module and to add capabilities beyond the TPM 2.0 specification. The hardware includes a secure element with a trusted execution environment. Firmware authorized by Microsoft is stored in the motherboard's SPI flash and loaded at boot, and Windows uses the newest available version. Updates arrive through Windows Update or classic UEFI capsule updates. Pluton is documented for Windows 11 on supported editions such as Pro, Enterprise and Education, with listed AMD, Intel and Qualcomm processors. A typical use is acting as the system TPM and supporting device-based conditional access in Intune, where device health is confirmed through tamper-resistant, cryptographically verifiable logs. That conditional access benefit applies only when Pluton is configured as the TPM.

microsoft-purview-records-management.title: Learn about records management – Microsoft Purview
microsoft-purview-records-management.notes: Records management in Microsoft Purview helps organizations handle content that has regulatory, legal or business-critical importance. It supports meeting legal obligations, demonstrating compliance and disposing of content that no longer needs to be kept. Retention labels can mark items as a record or a regulatory record, applied manually or automatically based on sensitive information, keywords or content types. Organizations can import or build a file plan, define retention periods based on creation or modification date, and use event-based retention that starts when a trigger occurs. Disposition reviews, proof of deletion and export of deleted items support the end of the lifecycle. Specific roles control access to records manager functions. A locked record blocks editing and deletion in SharePoint and OneDrive, while a regulatory record is stricter: the label cannot be removed or changed, not even by a global administrator, and retention can only be extended. Regulatory records must be enabled with PowerShell first and cannot come from auto-labeling policies. Exchange only follows locked-record behavior. The page also describes verifying migrated files by comparing hash values. Licensing is covered elsewhere in the documentation.

operator-connect.title: Plan for Operator Connect – Microsoft Teams
operator-connect.notes: Operator Connect links Microsoft Teams Phone to the public switched telephone network through a Microsoft-certified operator. The operator runs the PSTN infrastructure, while administrators manage users in the Teams admin center. The aim is simpler Teams Phone deployment without running and maintaining your own session border controllers, and it lets an organization keep working with an existing operator that participates in the program. Admins enable the chosen operator in the Teams admin center, assign phone numbers, buy new numbers, port existing ones or migrate users from another Teams Phone PSTN option. Prerequisites include the required Teams Phone licenses, users in Teams Only mode, suitable admin permissions, a certified operator available in the target countries or regions and a network that meets Teams requirements. Onboarding runs through four steps: check prerequisites, choose an operator, plan a number strategy and configure Operator Connect. Responsibilities are split. Microsoft covers Teams services and administration, while the operator handles PSTN connectivity, number provisioning and porting, calling services and PSTN-related support. Operator Connect is only one of several PSTN connectivity options.

policy-tip.title: Data loss prevention policy tips reference – Microsoft Purview
policy-tip.notes: A policy tip is a notice shown by a data loss prevention policy to tell users that the content they work with conflicts with a DLP rule. The reference describes where such tips appear and how they differ by application. In Outlook there are default and customized oversharing dialogs, a wait-on-send dialog and a custom compliance link for further user education, with availability depending on the client. In Teams, a flagged message shows a prompt where users can review the detected sensitive information types and, if the admin allows it, override or report a mistake. Supported conditions include content shared from Microsoft 365, sensitive information types, sensitivity labels, subject or body keywords and sender or recipient conditions. Support varies widely: policy tips work in SharePoint and OneDrive on the web, Office apps on the web for documents already stamped by a policy, Teams messages, endpoint devices and Fabric and Power BI. They are not available in SharePoint and OneDrive desktop clients, mobile Office apps, third-party cloud apps or on-premises content. Teams files get no tips, and Windows Office apps show them only for a limited set of conditions and actions.

provisioned-throughput-units.title: Provisioned throughput – Microsoft Foundry
provisioned-throughput-units.notes: A provisioned throughput unit is the unit of measure for provisioned deployments in Microsoft Foundry, where each unit represents a fixed amount of model processing capacity. The chosen number of units is reserved exclusively for the deployment whether or not requests arrive, giving predictable latency compared with standard deployments that share capacity. The page positions it for steady traffic, latency-sensitive applications, high production volumes and real-time scenarios such as chats, copilots or agents. Quota is model-independent but granted per subscription, region and deployment type, and each model has a minimum unit count and its own tokens-per-minute yield per unit. Billing is hourly per unit regardless of tokens consumed, with Azure Reservations as a discounted commitment option. Deployment types include global, data zone and regional provisioned. An optional spillover feature sends overflow requests to a standard deployment, but it is not available for every model family. Sizing relies on request rates, prompt and response sizes and cache rates, supported by a capacity calculator in the portal. Quota does not guarantee capacity, which can fluctuate, and reservations do not guarantee it either, so creating the deployment first is advised.
